pages.text: There was no shade in the yard below the wall. Grandma gave Yuki a large cloth and a rope. Momo plopped onto the cloth.
"I'll put up a canopy and play under it." Yuki picked up the rope.
Yuki tied one end tightly to the tree. The other sagged all the way to the wall.
The cloth drooped and dragged on the ground. Momo caught the rope in their mouth, pulled, and lost it. "You don't have hands, Momo."
Grandma watched from the porch. "Shall I hold the end?" Yuki pulled it closer and hid it behind their back.
Yuki wound the rope this way and that. It twisted and twisted.
The knot grew as big as a fist. The cloth slid to one side, making no shade. Sweat dotted Yuki's forehead.
Grandma gently untied the knot. "You needed a hand to hold the rope's end."
"Please hold that end, Grandma." She held the end by the wall. Yuki pulled the tree side taut.
A rectangle of shade appeared beneath the canopy. Momo sat inside with tongue hanging out.
